To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the oxygen affinity of the blood of tammar wallabies is higher in the prenatal than in the neonatal stage and (b) the oxygen affinity is higher in the neonatal than in the adult tammar.

(1) tammar blood 1-3 days prior to birth has a high P50, about 50 Torr, and a low delta log P50/ delta log PCO2 (about 0.2), (2) the Hill coefficient is high (nH > 3.5), and (3) there is a bend in the Hill plot at 50% saturation.
the P50 of the blood of the marsupial tammar wallaby fetus 1-2 day before birth is higher than in the mother and the neonate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxygen transport properties of the red cells of the marsupial tammar wallaby.
the physiological adaptations of the marsupial neonate and in this paper we report for the first time measurements of oxygen carriage in the blood of a prenatal marsupil.
the physiological and biochemical characteristics of the blood and its components during the early stages of development of the tammar wallaby, Macropus eugenil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the haemoglobin of the tammar wallaby has the same oxygen affinity as the adult at a given pH, PCO2 and temperature, but that the neonate and prenatal are different from the adult in their response to changes of PCO2.

the OECs of tammar wallabies show that the blood oxygen affinity is higher in prenatals than in adults, and that there is a change in oxygen affinity during the first 2-3 days after birth, which is associated with the disappearance of the fetal haemoglobins.
tammar haemoglobin is functionally different from that of eutherians.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the tammar wallaby, at the prenatal stage, there is a higher P50, lower nH and a lower delta log P50/ delta log PCO2 than in the adult.
tammar haemoglobins show a high affinity for oxygen, a low interaction between oxygen and CO2 carriage, aggregation of tetramers and four haemoglobins in the neonate and prenatals.

the haemoglobin of the prenatals has a high oxygen affinity, with a low delta log P50/ delta log PCO2, and a high nH, all suggesting a high oxygen affinity in the neonates, and that the haemoglobins of prenatals and neonates are identical to each other and to those of the adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen equilibrium curve of tammar blood is not like that of eutherian mammals.
the blood oxygen affinity of the tammar wallaby is much higher at the time of birth than at any other time in its life.
the high P50 and low CO2 sensitivity of the prenatals is not due to an immature haemoglobin.
